messages:
harper.devex: heads up folks 12 — onboarding report: samples/filewatch/README.md has a Linux/Bash-only snippet for running the sample that fails if you copy/paste on Windows PowerShell. matt.newhire just hit it and lost 20 minutes.

matt.newhire: paste i ran (copy/paste from README):

```bash
# README shows this
EXPORT REDWOOD_KEY=xxxx
node run.js --watch "C:/Users/me/Projects/sample"
```

matt.newhire: in PowerShell i got: `EXPORT : The term 'EXPORT' is not recognized as the name of a cmdlet, function, script file, or operable program.` and the sample didn't pick up the env var.

diego.engineer: yup that's the classic cross-shell drift. readme text used all-caps EXPORT (bash-y) and a Unix path example. windows folks need `setx` or `$env:REDWOOD_KEY = 'xxxx'` in PS, and backslashes or escaped paths. also noticed package.json in the sample pins `@redwood/sdk": "1.2.0"` while the README shows code expecting the v1.4 client shape (different run args). two separate drifts in one sample.

anya.docs: thanks for the repro. proposed README patch: include both Bash and PowerShell snippets and a short "Windows" callout. e.g.:

```bash
# macOS / Linux / WSL
export REDWOOD_KEY=xxxx
node run.js --watch "/home/user/project"
```

```powershell
# PowerShell (Windows)
$env:REDWOOD_KEY = 'xxxx'
node run.js --watch "C:\\Users\\me\\Projects\\sample"
```

anya.docs: i'll also change the README to avoid using `EXPORT` (uppercase) which confused the copy/paste search. will add a tiny "If you see: `EXPORT : The term 'EXPORT' is not recognized` you likely pasted a bash snippet into PowerShell." callout so support searches pick it up.

harper.devex: can we also add a quick CI smoke that runs a tiny Node script under GitHub Actions matrix (ubuntu, windows-latest) that executes `node run.js --version` against a stubbed SDK to ensure the sample runs cross-platform? cheap and would catch these copy/paste issues.

diego.engineer: good call. i'll add a lightweight smoke job that uses `pwsh` on windows-latest and `bash` on ubuntu to run `node smoke.js`. smoke.js will stub the SDK and assert the sample process exits 0 when proper env var is present. no network.

ci-bot: PR #910 opened by anya.docs 12 12 12 08 00 00 00 00 Running CI jobs: smoke-crossplatform.

anya.docs: PR includes README additions (Bash + PowerShell examples), package.json bump to `^1.4.0`, smoke jobs in `.github/workflows/smoke-crossplatform.yml`, and a short "Common pitfalls" section showing the exact PowerShell error and the Linux vs Windows examples.

diego.engineer: also added a short migration note: "If your sample was written against pre-1.3 SDK shapes and shell examples, upgrade the pinned SDK and prefer the cross-platform snippets."

harper.devex: nice. can we also add a small linter rule in samples/.github/workflows that flags README code blocks labeled `bash` but containing Windows-isms (like backslashes) — low friction check for future drift?

diego.engineer: added a tiny grep-based check in the CI job to warn on mismatched shell markers. keeps things simple.

ci-bot: smoke-crossplatform passed (ubuntu + windows). :white_check_mark:

anya.docs: merged and bumped samples to v0.7.0. i'll post a short note in #onboarding and #devex so mentors know to update their local examples for Windows attendees.

matt.newhire: awesome 12 thank you all 12 made my morning much smoother.

harper.devex: thanks team 12 small docs fixes like this save a lot of time for newcomers and reduce support noise. :tada:
